newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates steady on selective trade.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates steady on selective trade.

text.p: Pakistan cotton prices were steady on Saturday amid selective buying by exporters and dealers said prices might rise in the next trading week.
"Demand from exporters has picked up, with some spinners also following their lead," one dealer said, adding that prices could firm as more buying by exporters was expected.
In the kerb market, MNH-93 variety was traded at 2,000 rupees ($49.39) per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
The private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said 26,811 bales had been exported to Asian markets in May.
Total raw cotton exports since the start of the season in September 1996 had reached 74,224 bales compared to 1.817 million bales in the same year-ago period, the KCA said.
